findings.title: Docs-map drift detection repeatedly rescans graph edges and source symbols
findings.what: For every declared document source, scanDocsMapDrift calls graph.edges.some(), making reference validation O(declaredSources × graphEdges). It also rebuilds a Set from file.symbols for every source declaration, even when declarations reuse the same source file. Large docs-map and repo-map artifacts therefore cause avoidable N× detector latency.
findings.fix: Before iterating docs-map declarations, build one Set keyed by normalized source-reference owner and path, and cache one symbol-name Set per normalized repo-map file. Use constant-time membership checks inside the declaration loops.
findings.acceptance: Add a regression test proving identical findings with repeated source declarations, plus a scaling probe where multiplying documents, sources, and edges by 10 stays within a declared near-linear runtime budget rather than approaching quadratic growth.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read at the immutable baseline confirmed the nested loops at lines 785 and 796, the complete graph.edges.some scan at lines 801-807, and per-declaration symbol Set construction at line 831. Existing node and file maps do not eliminate either repeated operation; the claim is limited to this reproducible complexity defect.
